name: Alcyone
description: A star 135 parsecs away, 15 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: radius 13.762 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 843.922 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.91) and temperature; scaled from the paper's distance, 123.609 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 13.762 x 134.84/123.609 = 15.013 solar radii (luminosity 1004.3)

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: effective temperature 8392 +/- 4070 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.113)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 4 from 2001A&A...378..861C; the 1 published value span log g 4 to 4, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 66714384142368256 (quality B), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none

distance.source: Adopted Pleiades model geometry: normal depth 136.7 pc, 0.7 pc beyond the dust model's normal-depth reference of 136.0 pc along ICRS RA 56.67978318 deg, Dec 24.10845447 deg. Individual bright-star depths and their common plane are assumptions; measured sky positions, observed photometry and published parallax/facts remain separate.

color.companion: The Washington Double Star catalogue (Mason et al. 2001, AJ 122, 3466; VizieR B/wds/wds) lists Alcyone as WDS 03475+2406 OCC 251 Aa,Ab, a pair found by lunar occultation whose separation is not measured, of magnitudes 3 and 4.6: no spectrograph separates them, so the measured spectrum, and the color, are of both, the companion giving about 18.6% of the light.

text.card: A star 135 parsecs away, 15 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,004 times the Sun's luminosity at 8,392 K, so 15.013 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 17702: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Alcyone (star)
quotes.card: The star has the Bayer designation Eta Tauri, Latinized from η Tauri and abbreviated Eta Tau or η Tau.
